input.question: After World War 2 how did America end up with their economy improved and the rest of the world ended up broke?
input.ground_truth: America didn't get bombed and saw *immense* federal spending that ended the great depression. Also, as it turns out, being the only industrial power that didn't get bombed to hell makes your economy pretty strong as there isn't a whole lot of competition.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: After World War 2 how did America end up with their economy improved and the rest of the world ended up broke?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and your friends are playing a big game. You all have some toys and candies to start with. But then, a big storm comes (that’s like World War 2). Everyone loses some toys and candies because of the storm.

Now, after the storm, one of your friends (that’s America) still has lots of candy factories and toy makers. While the storm destroyed many factories and toys in other places, your friend’s factories are still standing and can make lots of new toys and candies really fast.

Also, after the storm, lots of people want to buy toys and candies from your friend because they know your friend’s toys are good and safe. So, your friend sells a lot and gets even more candies and toys!

But the other friends’ factories are broken, and they don’t have enough to make new toys or candies quickly. So, they don’t have as many candies or toys as before, and they are sad because they don’t have enough to share or play with.

That’s why, after the big storm (World War 2), America had lots of candies and toys (money and goods), but many other countries didn’t have as much.
